tagline: Out to White Hall, and over the mountain by Monticello.
intro: Two roads make up this byway. Garth Road runs between Charlottesville and the crossroads of White Hall by way of Owensville, and it carries U.S. Bike Route 76 as well as cars. Thomas Jefferson Parkway, SR 53, leaves SR 20 just south of the city, climbs Carters Mountain and winds over the summit between Monticello and Montalto, then comes down to the hamlet of Simeon, where a side road leads to James Monroe's estate.
The parkway became a state highway in 1930 and took the number 53 in 1947.

moments.title: White Hall
moments.text: The crossroads answered to Glenn's Store, Maupin's Tavern, Shumate's Tavern and a few other names before settling on White Hall in 1835.

moments.title: Our Lady of the Angels Monastery
moments.text: Six Trappistine nuns came in 1987 to a cheese farm with its old machinery still in place, and with help from neighbors they were making Gouda by 1990.

moments.title: Michie Tavern
moments.text: William Michie opened his tavern at Earlysville in 1784, and in 1927 it was taken down and moved seventeen miles to the parkway, close by Monticello.
